p114.lead: An isolated world, yet not forgotten: the superhuman government that watches over Urantia, the twelve corps of master seraphim, and the reserve corps of destiny.

p114.foot.text: Presented by the Chief of Seraphim stationed on Urantia

p114.s0.h: Introduction — The Unseen Hand in the Kingdoms of Men
p114.s0.b0: Paper 113 described the guardian angel at one person’s side; Paper 114 shows the superhuman government that cares for a whole planet. The author, the Chief of Seraphim stationed on Urantia, even gives the result of that day’s noon roll call: hundreds of millions of pairs of seraphim are at work on this world. Ably assisted by the midwayers, the angels carry out the mandates of the resident governor general and his subordinates.
p114.s0.b2: The planetary government of Urantia is unlike that of any other world in Satania, or even in all Nebadon. The author traces this uniqueness to seven unusual circumstances.

p114.s1.h: I. The Sovereignty of Urantia — Michael and the Vicegerent Prince
p114.s1.b0: The sovereignty of Urantia was first held in trust by the sovereign of the Satania system, and after the downfall of Caligastia the planet had no settled relationship with the local universe. When Michael completed his bestowal in the flesh, the Union of Days proclaimed him Planetary Prince of Urantia, and this forever settled the status of our world.
p114.s1.b1: Michael, however, does not administer the planet personally; he entrusted it to a Jerusem commission of twenty-four former Urantians. Machiventa Melchizedek has recently been designated vicegerent Prince but has not yet taken up his duties. Celestial beings differ on when he will come, and the author himself looks for his appearance any day or hour.
p114.s2.h: II–III. The Board of Planetary Supervisors; The Resident Governor General
p114.s2.b0: The twenty-four counselors on Jerusem were all real leaders during their lives on earth, and their leadership has been deepened by mansion world experience. When the council now sits, its chairman is John, known to us as “the Baptist.” They also advise the thirty-six other rebellion-isolated worlds of Satania.
p114.s2.b1: Every hundred years the council sends one of its members to Urantia to serve as **resident governor general**. While these narratives were being prepared, the nineteenth was succeeded by the twentieth. The governor general has no personal authority, yet each day he hands down scores of rulings that all concerned accept as final.
p114.s2.b2: He is the co-ordinating director recognized by every order of angelic host, and since the departure of 1-2-3 the first, the United Midwayers have looked upon the successive governors general as their planetary fathers. The council keeps in close touch with Michael through the Brilliant Evening Star who attended Jesus throughout his mortal bestowal. No one knows how long the counselors will serve as they do now; it will likely continue until some change such as the end of a dispensation, the final adjudication of the rebellion, or Michael’s return.
p114.s2.b5: The reason for withholding the name holds a lesson for us today. Respect for outstanding people slides easily into veneration, and then we end up looking at a person instead of at God.
p114.s3.h: IV–V. The Most High Observer; The Planetary Government
p114.s3.b0: Shortly after the rebellion the Most Highs of Edentia seized certain planetary authority, and so a Vorondadek Son still resides here as the Most High observer. In grave crises he may take over the planetary government, and this has happened thirty-three times in the history of Urantia. In purely spiritual matters, though, the supreme authority seems to rest with the commanding archangel at the divisional headquarters of the archangels.
p114.s3.b1: The Most High observer keeps close advisory relations with the planetary supervisors and also serves as advisory director of the race commissioners, who are very active on Urantia. Such Vorondadek regencies are not limited to rebel worlds: the Most Highs may intervene on any inhabited planet to bring the superior wisdom of the constellation rulers into the kingdoms of men. Unseen wisdom stands behind the great currents of history.
p114.s3.b2: The actual administration of Urantia is hard to describe in terms of a formal separation of powers. The structure the text describes can be summarized like this.

p114.s3.b4: This loosely organized government works better than expected thanks to the circuit of the archangels, which can be used in an emergency to get around the planet’s spiritual isolation. And above all, isolation matters little to the individual.
p114.s3.b6: Each administrative day on Urantia begins with a consultative conference attended by the governor general, the planetary chief of archangels, the Most High observer, the supervising supernaphim, the chief of resident Life Carriers, and invited guests. Most problems involving seraphim and midwayers are settled by mutual consent, and even the governor general’s rulings may be appealed to conciliating commissions or to the System Sovereign. The unseen government, too, follows the fair processes of consultation and appeal.
p114.s4.h: VI. The Master Seraphim of Planetary Supervision — Twelve Corps for Every Sphere of Life
p114.s4.b0: When the Spirit of Truth was poured out, the first governor general arrived accompanied by twelve corps of special seraphim, graduates of Seraphington. These are the master seraphim of planetary supervision, and the twelve acting chiefs of their groups form the governor general’s cabinet. The author, a supernaphim of the primary order, presides over this council.

p114.s4.b2: The progress angels and the religious guardians hold each other in check. One labors to make things what they ought to be; the other carries the imperishable values of old and passing forms into new patterns. The tension between change and conservation is a condition of healthy civilization.
p114.s4.b4: None of these angelic groups controls its domain arbitrarily. They manipulate conditions and associate circumstances so as to exert a favorable influence. They act as ideational clearinghouses, mind focalizers, and project promoters, but they do not push into the human mind ideas that are not there.
p114.s5.h: VII. The Reserve Corps of Destiny — Unknown Servants
p114.s5.b0: The reserve corps of destiny consists of living men and women admitted to the service of the superhuman administration of world affairs. As soon as someone appears with sufficient mental capacity, adequate moral status, and requisite spirituality, that person is assigned as a mortal assistant to a celestial group and given personal destiny guardians. Urantia has twelve reserve corps, one for each of the twelve groups of seraphic supervision.

p114.s5.b2: The corps now numbers 962 persons, and apart from fewer than a score of contact personalities, none of them knows they are being prepared for planetary crises. They are trained in the deep mind by the combined technique of Adjuster and seraphic ministry and emerge only in rare emergencies, to prevent the breakdown of culture or the extinction of the light of living truth. The text adds that it was through just such a combination of cosmic adjustments that these revelations were materialized in English.
p114.s5.b3: Reservists also act, unknowingly, as conservators of essential planetary information. When a reservist dies, vital data are often passed to a younger successor through a liaison of the two Adjusters. The corps has no permanent head but has permanent councils, among them the judiciary council, the historicity council, and the council on political sovereignty, and from time to time titular heads are commissioned for a task lasting a few hours. Membership was largest in the days of the Adamites and Andites, lowest around Pentecost, and has grown steadily since.
p114.s5.b5: The author admits that Urantia is far from an ideal planetary government. Compared with the other isolated worlds, though, it is not greatly inferior, and sweeping changes are expected when Michael comes again, if not before.
p114.s6.b0: Paper 114 ends in comfort. Urantia was isolated by rebellion, but it is not a cosmic orphan. From Uversa to Paradise they all know we are here, and the people of this world are cherished as lovingly as if it had never been betrayed—even more so.

p114.s6.b4: The next paper, Paper 115, “The Supreme Being,” turns fully to the Supreme Being—mentioned in Paper 113 as the one in whom the many celestial ministries are integrated—the evolving Deity of time and space.
p115.lead: A God with whom we must do as well as be: the relativity of concept frames, the Original, the Actual, and the Potential, and the source and nature of the Supreme Being who grows in time.

p115.foot.text: Sponsored by a Mighty Messenger temporarily sojourning on Urantia

p115.s0.b0: With Paper 115 begin three papers on the **Supreme Being**. Sponsored by a Mighty Messenger temporarily sojourning on Urantia, it opens by contrasting two relationships. With the Father, sonship is what counts; with God the Supreme, achievement is the prerequisite to status.
p115.s0.b2: This short sentence is the key to the whole paper. The Father’s love is a free gift, but the Supreme is a Deity who grows through what Creators and creatures actually achieve in experience. It follows that our efforts and accomplishments do not vanish in the universe; they become part of a divine reality.
p115.s1.h: I. Relativity of Concept Frames — Serviceable Scaffolding
p115.s1.b0: A partial and evolving intellect would be helpless in the universe without its innate ability to form a frame in which to think. When mind cannot reach true origins, it postulates conclusions and invents origins so that it can reason logically within that frame. Such frames are indispensable to rational thought, yet without exception they are more or less in error.
p115.s1.b1: Our understandings of truth, beauty, goodness, love, time, space, and even Deity are only relatively true. Concepts are scaffolding that must give way as comprehension expands. This humility does not weaken faith; it leaves room to imagine higher frames instead of being imprisoned in our present understanding.

head: Level of reality
Character
How possibilities become actual
rows: All-inclusive — even of the possibility of finite experience
Derived from and qualifying absolute reality
Exists by the eternal purpose of God

p115.s1.b5: A finite creature cannot explain its own existence without appealing to the prior acts and pre-existent will of its Creators. The final answer to the question “Why am I here?” is not logic but the will of God. Even the Father-Son concept will be enlarged by higher conceptions attained in Orvonton, Havona, and Paradise. For now we think within a mortal frame, but we can envision that higher frames exist.
p115.s2.h: II. The Absolute Basis for Supremacy — New Experience within Infinity
p115.s2.b0: From the existential standpoint nothing new can happen in the universe, for the completion of infinity is eternally present in the seven Absolutes. From a finite creature’s viewpoint, however, infinity holds much that is still only potential. The whole scheme of creation and evolution is the conversion of potentialities of space, mind, and spirit into actualities.
p115.s2.b1: We cannot comprehend how the value of anything infinite and divine could increase; yet in the experiential universes even divine values grow as actualities through enlarged comprehension of the meanings of reality. The possibility of such experiential growth becomes a universe actuality through triodity relationships that impinge upon the Supreme.
p115.s3.h: III. Original, Actual, and Potential — Growth Without End
p115.s3.b0: No language is adequate to express infinity. Since mind cannot form a concept without first breaking the unity of a reality, it postulates three phases in order to grasp the infinite. The intellect reaches its limit in the concept of the Supreme Being, but the spirit reaches beyond in worship.
p115.s3.b1: Infinity is unity on one side and endless diversity on the other. No creature can understand how a unity becomes duality, triunity, and diversity while remaining one. We meet the same problem when we think of the undivided Trinity alongside the plural personalization of God. Beyond the Supreme, concepts become more and more names and less and less true designations of reality.

p115.s3.b4: The interassociation of these three yields tensions within infinity that make all universe growth possible. In the originality of the First Source and Center, we cannot say that either actuality or potentiality exists or emerges. He simply is.
p115.s3.b5: From a creature’s viewpoint, actuality is substance and potentiality is capacity. Actuality expands from the center outward into infinity; potentiality comes inward from the periphery and converges at the center. The personality of the spirit Son is the master pattern of all personality, and the substance of the Paradise Isle is revealed perfectly in Havona and progressively in the superuniverses. So too with us: in seeking the actuality of Deity, we evolve the potential divinity within ourselves.
p115.s3.b7: The potential may fail to actualize in part, in time, but never in the aggregate. And because both the Actual and the Potential are encircuited in the I AM, growth has no end. Each human decision actualizes a new reality and at the same time opens a new capacity for growth.
p115.s3.b10: From a circumscribed view there are many endings, but from a higher view there are only transitions from one phase to another. That is why the philosophers of the universe have concluded that there is no such thing as an end. What looks like failure or loss may, from a longer perspective, be a doorway to the next stage.
p115.s4.h: IV–V. Sources of Supreme Reality; Relation of the Supreme to the Paradise Trinity
p115.s4.b0: Any consideration of the origin of God the Supreme must begin with the Paradise Trinity, for the Trinity is original Deity and the Supreme is derived Deity. The Supreme Being receives different aspects from different sources.

p115.s4.b2: It is hard to grasp how the infinite is actually manifest to the finite. Yet the evidence lies within us: the indwelling Adjuster is lasting proof that the absolute God can make direct contact with the least of all will creatures.
p115.s4.b4: Total finite reality is growing dynamically between the unqualified potentials of outer space and the unqualified actuals at the center of all things. When the Architects of the Master Universe have matured the possibilities of the potential Absolutes, the Supreme Creator Personalities emerge from Paradise to undertake the agelong task of bringing the evolving universes into being. Even the birth of a universe has its order of preparation and execution.
p115.s4.b5: The Supreme Being depends absolutely on the Trinity for the reality of his spirit nature. The Trinity remains forever the center of perfect and infinite stability, around which the evolutionary growth of the Supreme unfolds. As the age of Havona gives way to the age of the superuniverses, direct creation by the Trinity gives way to the creative acts of the children of the Paradise Deities.
p115.s5.h: VI. Relation of the Supreme to the Triodities — A Twofold Motion
p115.s5.b0: Paradise gravity, the spirit gravity of the Son, and the mind gravity of the Conjoint Actor still act directly. But the farther creation moves into uncharted space, the more it depends on developments within the three Absolute potentialities. The Supreme grows as creatures attain Godlikeness and as the finite possibilities are mastered.

p115.s5.b2: Just as the motion of the invisible can be discerned by its effects on the visible, the author says, the movements of Supremacy are detected by their repercussions in the personalities and patterns of the grand universe. The journey of a single ascending person is part of this vast inward motion.
p115.s6.h: VII. The Nature of the Supreme — The Finite Shadow of the Infinite
p115.s6.b0: In the Supreme, the Father has achieved relative liberation from the limitations of infinity, eternity, and absoluteness. The price is that the Supreme becomes subject to the necessity of experience and meets the barriers of time. It is precisely because he is partial and incomplete that he can know growth and development.
p115.s6.b2: The Supreme Being is the personification of the finite shadow cast across the grand universe by the infinite unity of the Paradise Father. He is the focalizer and unifier of evolutionary experience, and all this appears to contribute to the eventuation of God the Ultimate. The Supreme can be fully appreciated only by considering his source in the Trinity, his field of activity in the universe, and his destiny in the Trinity Ultimate.

p115.s6.b4: By summing up evolutionary experience, the Supreme connects the finite with the absonite, much as the mind of the Conjoint Actor integrates the spirituality of the Son with the energies of Paradise. The author concludes that all this unity must be a revelation of the original unity of the First Father-Cause of all things and beings.
p115.s7.b0: Paper 115 is full of abstract language, but its conclusion is close to home. The Supreme Being grows through experience built on effort, perseverance, and faith. Our honest efforts and patient growth therefore carry cosmic meaning. Concepts may change one day, but the spirit that reaches the Father in worship goes beyond their limits.

p115.s7.b2: The next paper, Paper 116, “⟦Q 115:4.7⟧The Almighty Supreme⟦/Q⟧,” examines the power aspect of the Supreme Being—how control and sovereignty evolve in the universes of time and space.
p116.lead: An imperfect world is the work of finite Creators: a Deity growing in power and personality, God the Sevenfold, spirit dominance, and the grand universe as a living organism.

p116.foot.text: Sponsored by a Mighty Messenger temporarily sojourning on Urantia

p116.s0.h: Introduction — The Religious Paradox of Inequality
p116.s0.b0: Paper 116 deals with the power aspect of the Supreme Being, the **Almighty Supreme**. The author begins with an old question: if God is perfect, why is the world so imperfect and unequal? The perfect spheres of Havona point to a perfect Creator, but the turmoil of Urantia leads honest reason to conclude that this world was made and is managed by Creators who are subabsolute and other than perfect.
p116.s0.b1: Once we recognize that our immediate Creators are divine yet finite, and that the God of time and space is an evolving Deity, inequality ceases to be a profound religious paradox. Then, says the text, faith will no longer be used to justify inequality.
p116.s0.b3: Havona does not grow; like the eternal Gods, it simply is. But growth characterizes the grand universe, and growth means partnership between creature and Creator. The Almighty Supreme is a living, evolving Deity of power and personality whose destiny is perfection but whose present experience includes growth and incompleteness.
p116.s0.b5: The Supreme Being functions first in the central universe as a spirit personality, and second in the grand universe as God the Almighty, a personality of power. His third function, in the master universe, is still latent, and the authors admit that none of them really knows what it will disclose.
p116.s1.h: I. The Supreme Mind — Progress That Never Stops
p116.s1.b0: The experience of every evolving creature is a phase of the experience of the Almighty Supreme. Joining power and personality is the function of the Supreme Mind, and the completed Almighty Supreme will be one unified, personal Deity, not a loose association of attributes. During the evolutionary ages the physical power potential rests with the Seven Supreme Power Directors and the mind potential with the Seven Master Spirits.
p116.s1.b1: The author confesses to knowing less about the mind of Supremacy than about any other aspect of this Deity. But one thing is certain: the body may complete its growth and spirit may reach perfection, but mind never stops progressing.
p116.s2.h: II. The Almighty and God the Sevenfold — The Stairway by Which Man Meets God
p116.s2.b0: Unqualified Paradise Deity is incomprehensible to the creatures of time and space, who grasp the meaning of divinity only through origins, relativities, and destinies. So Paradise Deity attenuates and qualifies itself, bringing the Supreme Creators into being, and its light finds its most distant and beautiful expression in the earth lives of the bestowal Sons. This is the origin of **God the Sevenfold**.
p116.s2.b2: One might infer that the first three levels together would equal Paradise Deity, but that is not so. Paradise Deity is existential, while the Supreme Creators express a new power potential of experiential Deity. God the Supreme originates in the Trinity, yet he becomes manifest to creatures as a personality of power only through the first three levels of God the Sevenfold.
p116.s3.h: III. The Almighty and Paradise Deity — Three Kinds of Participation
p116.s3.b0: The Paradise Deities act directly through their gravity circuits, but they also participate in the evolutions of time through various agencies. The text sets out side by side how each of the three Sources and Centers takes part.

p116.s3.b2: Michaels and Avonals live the actual creature life on the evolutionary worlds, adding bona fide creature natures to their divine natures. Here is revealed how the Supreme can be both creature and creator.
p116.s3.b4: The Adjusters are to human beings what the Trinity is to the Supreme Being: absolute foundations. On those foundations free choice evolves an eternal nature—a finaliter nature in man, a Deity nature in God the Supreme.
p116.s4.h: IV. The Almighty and the Supreme Creators — The Local Universe as Laboratory
p116.s4.b0: The unity of the Supreme Whole depends on the progressive unification of the finite parts. In this age the almighty power of the Supreme depends on the acts of God the Sevenfold, and Master Spirit Number Seven, who speaks for the Supreme, knows and is in personal contact with him. The Ancients of Days stand midway between Paradise and the evolving worlds, seeing both ways, knowing both ways, and co-ordinating both ways.
p116.s4.b1: Early in the superuniverse plan, when the Master Spirits joined the Trinity in creating the forty-nine Reflective Spirits, the Supreme Being also functioned creatively, and Majeston appeared. The collective creations of the Master Spirits are ordinarily quasi-material, but when they produced the Seven Circuit Spirits in response to the will of the Supreme, the offspring were spiritual. The purpose of the Supreme changed the very character of the creation.
p116.s4.b2: The real laboratories, though, are the local universes. There even the Creators evolve: the presence of the Conjoint Actor grows into a Universe Mother Spirit, and the Creator Son into the nature of experiential supreme sovereignty. Because the personalities farthest from God start there, the greatest spiritual ascent and the fullest experience of cocreating oneself are possible there.
p116.s4.b4: When a bestowal Son shows a new way to find God, he does not create the path; he lights up an everlasting highway that was always there. The text even says that mortal man appears to be necessary to the full function of God the Sevenfold.
p116.s5.h: V. The Almighty and the Sevenfold Controllers — The Struggle for Physical Equilibrium
p116.s5.b0: God the Sevenfold includes not only the creators but also the controllers of the grand universe. These seven groups form the physical-control level of this Deity association, and the Almighty Supreme is evolving as the overcontroller of the physical power of the grand universe.

p116.s5.b2: The struggle for perfection belongs not only to the levels of intellect and spirit but also to the level of energy and mass. Because new energy and new mass keep appearing, a growing universe is always unsettled. In the final analysis all energy responds to mind, and the total evolution of the universe is the personality unification of energy-controlling mind with spirit.
p116.s5.b3: In the early days of universe building even the Paradise Creators are chiefly concerned with material equilibrium, and the Creator Son does not leave his capital planet until the gross equilibrium of his local universe has been established. In universes settled in light and life there are no major unexpected physical events. Stability does not come by itself; it is won through long labor.
p116.s6.h: VI. Spirit Dominance — The Wider the Gulf, the Greater the Opportunity
p116.s6.b0: In the evolutionary superuniverses energy-matter dominates everywhere except in personality, where spirit, through mind, struggles for mastery. In relation to personality, physical systems are subordinate, mind systems co-ordinate, and spirit systems directive. This dominance of spirit grows through the freewill acts of Creators and creatures.

p116.s6.b2: Here is why our world is difficult. Where divinity is more attenuated, the problems are harder, but the opportunity to gain experience in solving them is larger too. When in a person mind guides the body and spirit leads the mind, a new child of the Supreme is born; and the growth of the parts gathers into the growth of the whole.
p116.s7.h: VII. The Living Organism of the Grand Universe — The Universe Compared to a Body
p116.s7.b0: The grand universe is not only a vast material creation; it is a responsive, living organism. The author explains it by comparison with the human body.

p116.s7.b2: One person’s effort to attain God sets up a divine tension in the universe, which is resolved by the evolution of an immortal soul. When all creatures and Creators strive together in this way, the resulting cosmic tension is resolved only in the synthesis of almighty power with the spirit person of the Supreme Being.
p116.s8.b0: Paper 116 invites us to read an imperfect world not as God’s failure but as a stage for growth. The confusion and inequality we meet are tasks that finite Creators and creatures must work out together, and in the process the Supreme Being himself grows. The way of faith, then, is neither resignation nor complacency in the face of inequality, but achieving our share of mastery.

p116.s8.b2: The next paper, Paper 117, “⟦Q 116:2.14⟧God the Supreme,⟦/Q⟧” is the last of the three papers on the Supreme Being, continuing the study of the evolving Deity whose power aspect this paper has explored.
p117.lead: The finite God who grows in time: the cosmic responsibility, and the comfort, of knowing that our choices and our growth take part in the actualization of the Supreme Being.

p117.foot.text: Sponsored by a Mighty Messenger temporarily sojourning on Urantia

p117.s0.h: Introduction — What Happens When We Do God’s Will
p117.s0.b0: Near the close of Part III, Paper 117 takes up the Supreme Being directly. Its author is a Mighty Messenger temporarily sojourning on Urantia, and its first sentence is the key to the whole paper: whenever anyone, anywhere, does the will of God, the potential of the Supreme becomes one step more actual.
p117.s0.b2: The will of God is the purpose of the First Source and Center. It exists in different ways on different levels of Deity, and God the Supreme is becoming the place where that will finds its highest expression in the finite.

head: Where
The will of God is
rows: Becoming the highest finite manifestation of the total will

p117.s0.b4: So on the day the whole universe fully lives the will of God, the time-space creations will be settled in light and life, and the personality of God the Supreme will emerge as fact. The parts of the grand universe grow as a reflection of the Supreme’s evolution, and the Supreme is the cumulative total of all that evolution.
p117.s1.h: I. Nature of the Supreme Being — The Deity Where Creator and Creature Meet
p117.s1.b0: The first section paints the Supreme in many aspects. He is the oversoul of the grand universe, the consciousness of the finite cosmos, and the personification of Creator-creature experience. Above all, he is where the three values of truth, beauty, and goodness come together in the finite.
p117.s1.b2: The Gods descend into time and space in the persons of the Supreme Creators, and creatures ascend in quest of the Father. This great procession of descent and ascent reveals the evolution of the Supreme, in whom those who descend and those who ascend come to understand each other and discover their brotherhood. The will of the Supreme therefore becomes something more than the will of either Creator or creature.
p117.s1.b3: The section makes room for human love too. When a person who has received the Father’s love revealed by Michael seeks to show that love to others, such creature affection is a true reflection of the love of the Supreme.
p117.s2.h: II. The Source of Evolutionary Growth — An Emptiness That Can Be Filled
p117.s2.b0: To mortal man, existence is equivalent to growth. The author holds that this growth is a function of the Supreme and is peculiar to the age of the Supreme’s growth. That is why not every being living in this age takes part in such growth.

head: Being
Relation to the growth of the Supreme
rows: Have experience and memory but do not grow as ascenders do — held in reserve for the next age
Status fixed by Trinity embrace, so experience does not issue in growth
In and of the Supreme, sharing his cycle of growth — hence the finaliter destiny
Growth potential beyond the superuniverses — not part of this age’s synthesis

p117.s2.b2: This contrast lets us see our place anew. Our incompleteness is an opportunity before it is a defect. Because the Supreme is not yet complete, there is room for creatures to grow and to add to his completion.
p117.s3.h: III. Significance of the Supreme to Universe Creatures
p117.s3.b0: As Jesus is the living way from self-consciousness to God-consciousness, so the Supreme is the living way from finite consciousness to what lies beyond it. The Creator Son could be such a way because he actually traveled it, from the humanity of Joshua ben Joseph to the divinity of Michael; likewise the Supreme is a way because he actually embodies the evolution of every creature.
p117.s3.b1: The author says that human growth and the Supreme’s growth are alike. Both depend on help from above, yet both take part willingly in their own completion. Deity is existential in the Trinity, experiential in the Supreme, and creature-realized in mortals through Adjuster fusion.

head: Comparison
God the Supreme
The immortal human soul
rows: The divinity successes of the creator and administrator children
The personality decisions of the human mind
A volitional participant in his own deity actualization
A cocreative partner in its own immortalization

p117.s3.b3: The Supreme did not create man, but man’s life was derived from his potentiality. He does not initiate original causation, but he appears to be the catalyzer of all universe growth.
p117.s4.h: IV. The Finite God — Divinity Placed in Human Hands
p117.s4.b0: Because God the Supreme is the finite Deity, he must deal with the problems of the finite himself. The struggles of creatures for perfection reflect the Supreme’s own struggle for self-realization. When a person chooses survival, the Supreme gains a wider experiential sovereignty; when someone rejects it, that part of the Supreme suffers inescapable delay.
p117.s4.b2: No choice can destroy the Adjuster, but the evolving self can be lost. All that was worthwhile in such a life persists, yet that personality never appears again, returning to the Supreme as a drop of water returns to the sea. However small the individual may seem beside the whole, each personality carries an irreplaceable meaning-value.
p117.s4.b3: From this comes **cosmic morality**. It transcends any temporal sense of relative right and wrong and rests on the creature’s recognition of an experiential obligation to experiential Deity. In a certain sense Supreme Deity depends on the choices of the mortal will, and so the author asks us again and again not to pass into the realm of the unrealized.
p117.s5.h: V. The Oversoul of Creation — What We Take and What We Leave
p117.s5.b0: A creature who submits to the Creator’s will does not lose his personality; he grows ever larger by sharing in this Deity adventure. At the same time, the repercussions of all human experience become part of the Supreme’s divine experience. When man acts, the Supreme reacts, and this exchange is progress itself.

p117.s5.b3: In the end, what we take with us is not the circuits but character. Decisions illuminated by sincere worship, glorified by intelligent love, and consummated in brotherly service accumulate into a cosmically moral character. The small decisions of each day become eternal capital.
p117.s6.h: VI. The Quest for the Supreme — Slowly, Like a River
p117.s6.b0: As God is our divine Father, so the Supreme is our divine Mother, in whom we are nurtured throughout our universe lives. The evolving soul is the child of the Adjuster’s action and of the Universal Mother’s reaction. Yet until the soul awakens, this assurance of kinship must be realized by faith.
p117.s6.b1: This section traces the circuit of love. Love comes from the Father, passes through sons to brothers, and so reaches the Supreme. It cannot be locked in the heart; it becomes real only when given to others.
p117.s6.b3: In the present age the only approach to the Supreme is through experience, and the text names three avenues. Paradise Citizens come to understand him by descending through Havona and exploring the work of the Supreme Creators; time-space ascenders draw near him as they traverse Havona; and Havona natives comprehend him through contact with pilgrims going both ways. Every avenue opens not through solitary thought but through living and meeting.

head: Comparison
Finding the Father

The great cause of spiritual ascent
The great effect of the Paradise career

p117.s6.b6: So the Supreme is found not suddenly like an earthquake but quietly and patiently, as a river wears away the soil. On that road a God-knowing person is never lonely, for the Father walks beside him and the very way he travels is the presence of the Supreme.
p117.s7.h: VII. The Future of the Supreme — A New Challenge after Completion
p117.s7.b0: When all finite potentials are realized, the Supreme will emerge as an almighty Deity presence. The author believes he will then be as personalized as the Eternal Son, as powerized as the Isle of Paradise, and as unified as the Conjoint Actor. Finaliters, in taking their oath to the Paradise Trinity, already pledge fidelity to God the Supreme.
p117.s7.b1: The author does not hide the problems inherent in this picture. The Supreme can hardly function fully before his evolution is complete, yet his Unqualified Supervisors already exercise a qualified sovereignty in universes settled in light and life. Where the finite touches the superfinite, the future may cast its image ahead—and the Thought Adjuster within us is a true prediction of future attainment in eternity.
p117.s7.b2: In that day the boundaries between the superuniverses will gradually disappear and the grand universe will function as a perfected whole. But rest will not last long: the enigma of the emerging God the Ultimate will challenge the perfected citizens anew. The author speaks of all this with care, as belief and conjecture rather than settled fact.
p117.s8.b0: Paper 117 may look like vast cosmology, but at its center stands one person’s choice. Each time we do God’s will, pass love on to others, and choose survival, our share is added to the growth of the finite God. No one else can make that contribution for us.

p117.s8.b2: The next paper, Paper 118, “Supreme and Ultimate—Time and Space,” carries forward the relationship between the Supreme and the Ultimate opened in this paper, in terms of time and space and the problems of creature will.
p118.lead: Time and space, causation and will, mechanism and providence: a philosophical study of the framework in which finite creatures live alongside the infinite God.

p118.foot.text: Sponsored by a Mighty Messenger temporarily sojourning on Urantia

p118.s0.h: Introduction — Seven Natures of Deity and Unending Growth
p118.s0.b0: Like Paper 117, Paper 118 was sponsored by a Mighty Messenger temporarily sojourning on Urantia. Where the previous paper portrayed God the Supreme himself, this one asks how the Supreme and the Ultimate are bound up with time and space, causation and will, and providence. It starts from a list that sets out the several natures of Deity at a glance.
p118.s0.b2: As God the Sevenfold is indispensable to the attainment of the Supreme, so the Supreme is indispensable to the emergence of the Ultimate. Together they form the experiential bridge linking the beginnings and completions of all creative growth in the master universe. The author explains this growth with an image from numbers: just as one can always be added to any number, growth has no end—yet it is punctuated by satisfying moments of goal attainment, and those moments become the prelude to new adventures.
p118.s1.h: I. Time and Eternity — The Time Unit of Maturity
p118.s1.b0: Absolute Deity is eternal by nature, but in the evolutionary universes eternity is experienced as the “everlasting now.” A mortal can become eternal by identifying with the indwelling spirit through choosing to do the Father’s will. The creature’s purpose then becomes fixed; a million or a billion moments make no difference.
p118.s1.b1: A distinctive insight of this section is that it describes maturity in terms of the length of one’s unit of time. We make decisions in the present by weighing past experience and future wisdom together. As the self matures, it reaches farther into past and future, and its decisions are freed more and more from the fetters of the moving present.

head: Comparison
Time unit of immaturity
Time unit of maturity
rows: Reveals the co-ordinate relation of past, present, and future
Divorces the present from past and future

p118.s1.b4: On infinite levels the present contains all the past and all the future. To God as absolute, an ascender who has made the eternal decision is already a finaliter. Yet through the Adjuster the Father does not stop at that knowledge; he takes part in every struggle of the creature rising from animallike to Godlike levels.
p118.s2.h: II–III. Omnipresence and Ubiquity; Time-Space Relationships
p118.s2.b0: God the Supreme may not be a demonstration of time-space omnipresence, but he is literally a manifestation of divine ubiquity. Ascenders discern God progressively through the ministry of God the Sevenfold, discover God the Supreme in Havona, find him as a person on Paradise, and as finaliters seek to know him as Ultimate. The assurance that whatever level they reach they will encounter the same Paradise Father keeps finaliters undisturbed.
p118.s2.b1: We perceive time by analysis and space by synthesis, and we join the two by the integrating insight of personality. Of all the animal world only man has this capacity. And truth rises above the conditions of time: the more truth we know and the more truth we are, the better we understand the past and grasp the future.
p118.s2.b3: When the eternal truth of the Creator is linked with the factual experience of the creature, a new value of the Supreme emerges. On space, the author is humble: space comes nearer than any other nonabsolute thing to being absolute, yet it is not absolute, and whether the pattern of an idea occupies space, he confesses, is really not known.
p118.s3.b0: Many theological difficulties arise from attributing infinite and absolute qualities to subordinate Divinity and to evolutionary Deity. There is a true First Cause, but there are also a host of co-ordinate and secondary causes. A first cause produces original effects that inherit nothing from antecedent causes; a secondary cause always yields effects that show inheritance from what went before.

p118.s3.b2: In the cosmic sense, then, Creator Sons are transformative creators, yet from the finite viewpoint they certainly do create. This distinction does not diminish God’s greatness; it gives his many co-workers their rightful place.
p118.s4.h: V–VI. Omnipotence and Compossibility; Omnipotence and Omnificence
p118.s4.b0: Omnipotence is not the power to do the nondoable. Even the infinite God does not make square circles or evil that is inherently good, for such contradictions amount to nonentity. Omnipotence not only creates things but gives origin to the very nature of things.
p118.s4.b2: In the beginning the Father does all, but as eternity unfolds, creatures—even men—become God’s partners in realizing destiny. Consciousness also flows in opposite directions. Man moves from fact to meaning to value; the Creator moves from thought-value through word-meaning to the fact of action. That is why God always seeks man first.
p118.s4.b4: God is omnipotent, but he is not **omnificent**. To claim that he personally does all that is done would disenfranchise nearly a million Creator Sons and their countless helpers. Human will, too, is relative: man cannot choose to be other than human, but he can choose to be more than a man. The choice to find God and be like him alone transcends finite limits. Recognizing omnipotence brings security; accepting omnificence leads into the error of pantheism.
p118.s5.h: VII. Omniscience and Predestination — Foreknowledge Does Not Erase Freedom
p118.s5.b0: The Master Architects have set the maximum limits within which will can operate, but within those bounds the sovereignty of creature will is not diminished. A wise adult may accurately forecast a younger associate’s decision without making that decision any less free. Mistaken choice is time bound, and it reveals the range of choice that immature creatures must be given if they are to make free contact with reality.
p118.s5.b2: True freedom carries even the possibility of self-destruction. So on the lower levels choice is narrowed for safety, and as one ascends the universes choice grows freer, until, in identification with God’s will, it approaches divine freedom.
p118.s6.h: VIII. Control and Overcontrol — The Time Governor and Self-Imposed Restraints
p118.s6.b0: Man is a living mechanism, but he is much more than a machine: he is mind endowed and spirit indwelt. He can never escape the chemical mechanics of the body, yet by consecrating his mind to the urges of the Adjuster he can increasingly subordinate that machine to the wisdom of experience.

head: State of choice
Result
rows: Stability at the expense of progress
Free of mechanism but unidentified with spirit
Liberation from the physical level together with divine stability

p118.s6.b2: There is a reason evolution is slow. Time is a brake on dangerous velocities of progress, and when material achievement outruns worship-wisdom, civilization carries the seeds of retrogression. The iniquity of Caligastia and of Lucifer lay in trying to break this time governor prematurely. So whenever we overcome an outward restraint, we must put in its place a voluntarily assumed restraint: concepts of justice and ideals of brotherhood.
p118.s7.h: IX. Universe Mechanisms — Time and Space That Insulate and Limit
p118.s7.b0: Time and space are the devices by which finite creatures can coexist with the Infinite. Without them no creature could act, yet by them every act is limited. Mechanisms are the fixed crystallizations of Creator thought and always function true to the concept that gave them origin; their purposiveness lies in their origin, not in their function.
p118.s7.b1: The grand universe is both mechanism and organism, a living mechanism. The author sums up God the Supreme as the personalization of all universe experience, the focalization of all finite evolution, and the consummation of cosmic wisdom. In the eternal future he will synthesize the manifold finite diversities into one meaningful whole.
p118.s8.h: X. Functions of Providence — A Slow and Sure Emergence
p118.s8.b0: Providence does not mean that everything has been decided in advance; that would be cosmic tyranny, not love. Providence works with regard to the total, and intervention occurs not because of a creature’s importance as a person but because of the importance of its function to the growth of some whole. Nevertheless, the Father as a person may at any time put a fatherly hand into the stream of events.
p118.s8.b2: What we call good luck may be bad luck, and an apparently cruel fate may be the tempering fire that forges character. Providence is partial and unpredictable, yet it is neither whimsical nor magical.

head: Factors that change the view of nature as heartless
What they involve
rows: Growing comprehension of material facts, meaningful ideas, and spiritual ideals
Accumulated knowledge of natural laws and spiritual purposes breaks down superstition
Growing insight and experience bring him nearer the unifying presence and harmony of Supremacy

p118.s8.b5: Providence becomes most evident on a world where people not only master material problems but begin to live according to the trend of the universes. The kingdom of God is in the hearts of men, and when it becomes real in the heart of every person on a world, the sovereignty of the Supreme Being is attained.
p118.s9.b0: Paper 118 is full of difficult philosophical terms, but beneath them lies a single message. We are limited by time and mechanism, yet those limits protect us, and when we identify ourselves with the will of God, true freedom and stability come together. Providence is not luck; it is the direction of the universe, revealed more and more to those who walk that way.

The teaching behind it

Do not stop at enduring; understand and forbear
Take on restraints of justice and mercy in proportion to your freedom

Suffering may be the tempering fire

The answer is often a changed attitude

p118.s9.b2: The next paper, Paper 119, “The Bestowals of Christ Michael,” is the last of Part III, and it carries all this cosmology into the concrete story of one Son’s seven bestowals.
p119.lead: From a Melchizedek to the babe of Bethlehem: how the Creator Son Michael seven times became one of his own creatures and earned his sovereignty by experience.

p119.foot.text: Presented by Gavalia, Chief of the Evening Stars of Nebadon

p119.s0.h: Introduction — Why Does a Creator Become a Creature?
p119.s0.b0: The author of Paper 119 is Gavalia, Chief of the Evening Stars of Nebadon. Sent by Gabriel to tell the story of the seven bestowals of Michael, the Universe Sovereign, he states at the outset that he will keep strictly to the limits of his commission. Bestowal is inherent in the Paradise Sons, and it began when the Eternal Son bestowed himself seven times on the seven circuits of Havona.
p119.s0.b1: A Creator Son vows to the Trinity not to assume full sovereignty of his universe until he has completed seven creature bestowals and been certified by the Ancients of Days. Bestowals are not essential to governing a universe efficiently, but they are absolutely necessary to governing a universe of imperfect creatures fairly, mercifully, and with understanding.

head: What a Creator Son has from the start
What the bestowal experience adds
rows: Mercy in new and additional ways
The real viewpoint of a creature, gained in the creature’s environment
Patience and fair judgment born of experiential creature existence

p119.s0.b4: Michael of Nebadon is the 611,121st bestowal of the Eternal Son upon time and space. He began organizing our universe about four hundred billion years ago and prepared for his first bestowal about one billion years ago; his bestowals came about one hundred and fifty million years apart, the last on Urantia nineteen hundred years ago.

p119.s1.h: I. The First Bestowal — A Strange Melchizedek
p119.s1.b0: Almost a billion years ago, Michael announced that his elder brother Immanuel would take charge of Nebadon while he was absent on an unexplained mission. Standing alone on the dispatching field, he said that many would wish to go with him but that this was something they could not do, and then he vanished from the sight of all.
p119.s1.b2: At noon on the third day, a strange Melchizedek Son, wholly like that order, appeared on the Melchizedek sphere accompanied by a solitary omniaphim. For a hundred years he served on emergency missions, and by universal consent he became chief of the Melchizedeks. The last words of the Melchizedeks’ record bear brief and warm witness to how the Creator lived among his creatures.
p119.s1.b4: The author notes that the records do not specifically name this Melchizedek as Michael, though it is universally believed that he was. The fact of the bestowals is known; the method is recorded only on Sonarington. This honest marking of limits runs through the whole paper.
p119.s2.h: II. The Second Bestowal — Savior Sovereign of a Rebel System
p119.s2.b0: The second bestowal took place in the midst of rebellion. After Lutentia, sovereign of system 11 in constellation 37, refused to accept a verdict and led a rebellion, Michael disappeared again, and three days later a new Son appeared among the Lanonandek reserves and became acting System Sovereign. He set the confused system in order with justice and mercy, and even offered to share the throne with the rebel if only he would apologize.
p119.s2.b1: Lutentia knew the stranger was Michael and spurned the offer, but millions of his misguided followers accepted forgiveness. The new ruler became known as the Savior Sovereign of Palonia, and on the day he left, even the rebel sent a message acknowledging him.
p119.s3.h: III. The Third Bestowal — Material Son on an Isolated World
p119.s3.b0: The third bestowal was on planet 217, in the system where Nebadon’s second rebellion had occurred. Michael held back the Life Carriers’ request and disappeared; on the third day a strange Material Son appeared with a seconaphim and was made acting Planetary Prince. On a world cut off from outside communication he worked alone for a whole generation and brought about the repentance and reclamation of the defaulting Planetary Prince and his staff.
p119.s3.b1: The author counts this reclamation among the most touching chapters in the salvation annals of Nebadon. Since then no Material Son or Daughter in Nebadon has complained of the difficulty of a mission, and none has knowingly joined a rebellion against Michael. Knowing that their sovereign went through the very trials they face has made their loyalty firm.
p119.s4.h: IV. The Fourth Bestowal — The Sovereign Disguised as a Seraphim
p119.s4.b0: In the fourth bestowal Michael became a supreme seraphim and for over forty years served as teaching counselor to twenty-six master teachers. Throughout that age every seraphim was regarded with special solicitude, since anyone might unknowingly have the Universe Sovereign as a colleague. His identity was established with certainty only at the end, when he was attached to the bestowal mission of a Trinity Teacher Son.
p119.s4.b1: As the bestowals descended toward lower forms of life, Gabriel became more closely involved, acting as liaison between the bestowed Michael and Immanuel, the acting ruler. Having lived the lives of three orders of his created Sons and of the angels, Michael now turned to the ascending career of his lowest will creatures, the evolutionary mortals.
p119.s5.h: V–VI. The Fifth and Sixth Bestowals — Walking the Path of the Ascending Mortal
p119.s5.b0: In the fifth bestowal Michael appeared on Uversa as Eventod, an unnumbered spirit pilgrim of mortal origin, and for eleven years was tested and tried just like his fellows. His first appearance in a stage of mortal evolution thrilled all Nebadon. Afterward the Melchizedek colleges began to teach the likelihood that Michael would one day come as a mortal of the flesh.
p119.s5.b1: The technique remained a mystery. Even Gabriel confesses that he does not understand how the Creator can take on the personality of one of his creatures and live its life. In the sixth bestowal Michael lived as a morontia mortal on Endantum; the author says it was one of the most extraordinary epochs of all his bestowals, but he is forbidden to reveal the details.
p119.s5.b2: Millions gathered on Salvington to welcome Michael back. Addresses of thanks poured in, but his reply was short and humble. By this time it was clear to all that their Creator had become a fellow creature.
p119.s6.h: VII. The Seventh and Final Bestowal — As a Helpless Infant
p119.s6.b0: Urantia was announced as the scene of the final bestowal shortly after the default of Adam and Eve became known. Apart from the mystery of incarnation, there was no secrecy about any step of this bestowal. What surprised everyone was that Michael came not fully grown, as before, but as a helpless infant.
p119.s6.b2: The author says this seemed the most precarious step of Michael’s career. A universe that knew of the Lucifer rebellion and the Caligastia disaffection could gauge the intensity of the struggle ahead. The baby Joshua ben Joseph was conceived and born like any other child and raised by ordinary parents in the manner of his time. The only supernatural event connected with his birth was the seraphim’s announcement to Ardnon and his associates.
p119.s7.h: VIII. Michael’s Postbestowal Status — Sovereignty Earned by Experience
p119.s7.b0: After the final bestowal Michael was proclaimed settled ruler of Nebadon, followed by the eighth proclamation from Uversa and a joint pronouncement from the Father and the Son. When the Trinity Sons were instructed to withdraw, Michael personally asked them to remain in Nebadon forever. He would not consent to the departure of the Sons of counsel and co-operation, and Paradise attached them permanently to his court.
p119.s7.b2: The seven bestowals augmented not only Michael’s sovereignty but also the sovereignty of God the Supreme. Each one revealed one of the wills of the Deities personalized in the Seven Master Spirits, and the titles Urantia gives him trace that same journey.

p119.s7.b5: Urantia thus became the sentimental shrine of all Nebadon and the mortal home of Christ Michael. This paper, the last of Part III, is the sixty-third of a series narrating the history of Urantia down to Michael’s appearance in the flesh, and it was written in A.D. 1935.
p119.s8.b0: Paper 119 shows that power cannot take the place of understanding. Even the Creator of a universe had to live as a creature before he could rule. Anyone placed in a position to lead or judge others can learn the humility of actually entering into their situation.

p120.lead: Immanuel’s charge to the departing Michael: the purpose and the limits of a final bestowal surrendered wholly to the Father’s will, and the one person who was both God and man.

p120.foot.text: Presented by the Melchizedek director of the revelatory commission

p120.s0.h: Introduction — The Price Paid for Sovereignty
p120.s0.b0: Paper 120 opens Part IV, “The Life and Teachings of Jesus.” Its author is the Melchizedek director of the revelatory commission appointed by Gabriel, and he tells of events just before Michael came to Urantia. He begins by saying that for a Creator Son to live the lives of his creatures is part of the price he pays for sovereignty.
p120.s0.b2: At any time Michael could have ruled Nebadon in his own right as a Creator Son. But rather than rule by isolated right, he wished to become a ruler who embodies the wisdom of the Supreme Being through actual experience of co-operative subordination to the Trinity. So the seven bestowals had a double purpose: to complete his understanding of creatures, and to represent the maximum authority of the Trinity.

head: Michael’s rule
Character
Basis
rows: Derived from experienced association with the Paradise Deities
Acquired through actual experience in the likeness of universe creatures
Embodies at once the sevenfold viewpoint of Deity and the creature viewpoint

p120.s0.b4: In this bestowal Michael chose to subject himself to the personal will of the Father. By that decision he would experience not only the nature of mortal man but also the will of the Father, and he could go with the assurance that Immanuel would keep the universe with the Father’s authority and that the Ancients of Days had decreed its safety.
p120.s0.b5: Having chosen the time and the planet, Michael held the usual conference with Gabriel and then presented himself before Immanuel, his elder brother and counselor. He turned over to Immanuel every administrative power not already given to Gabriel, and Immanuel, accepting the custody of the universe, began to impart the counsel that would guide Michael as he grew up a mortal. Most of this paper consists of permitted excerpts from that charge.
p120.s1.h: I. The Seventh Bestowal Commission — Depend Wholly on the Father
p120.s1.b0: Immanuel’s charge opens with trust in his brother. In the six earlier bestowals Michael had appeared fully grown, but now he would come to a disordered planet as a helpless babe. Immanuel calls this a new and untried experience.
p120.s1.b1: Immanuel points out the place of this bestowal. In the previous ones Michael had submitted to every phase of the will of the Supreme except the personal will of the Paradise Father. Now at last he had chosen to be wholly subject to the Father’s will, and meanwhile Immanuel would hold the universe as the Father’s personal representative.
p120.s1.b3: Michael had laid aside all extraplanetary support and every special help his creatures might give. As the creatures of Nebadon depend on him, so now he must depend on the Father. In this way he would come to know in his own experience the meaning of the faith-trust he had always asked of his creatures.
p120.s1.b5: Immanuel tells Michael that he need be concerned with only one thing: unbroken communion with the Father. Immanuel would see to the security of the universe, and by mandate of the Ancients of Days no rebellion could occur during the bestowal. The delegated authority could be reclaimed whenever Michael wished, but if he did so, Immanuel adds, it would be wholly for personal reasons.
p120.s2.h: II. The Bestowal Limitations — Nine Directions
p120.s2.b0: The second section contains the guidance Michael was to follow as he grew aware of his divine identity. What stands out is the request to accomplish in weakness what he could have done by power. Since Michael had refused to crush the rebels by his creator prerogatives, he was now to wrest dominion from them in the likeness of the lowest of his creatures.
p120.s2.b1: The second and third directions show that this life was not a matter for Urantia alone. If, as the Son of Man, he technically ended the Lucifer rebellion and received the title “⟦Q 120:2.2⟧Planetary Prince of Urantia,⟦/Q⟧” the whole universe would recognize the justice of doing in mortal flesh what mercy had kept him from doing by power. And after that, Immanuel says, similar challenges to his authority could never recur.

rows: Grow up as a child of the realm, complete your education, live by the Father’s will, and ascend to the Father

Remember that you remain potentially a Creator Son, and refrain from any superhuman will-to-power

p120.s2.b3: The fifth direction has a clear order. First liberate man’s spiritual nature; next illuminate the intellect, heal the soul, and free the mind from fear; and then, with wisdom, minister to physical well-being.
p120.s2.b5: The seventh direction says that this life was meant not as an example for the people of one age to copy, but as an inspiration to every generation on every world of Nebadon. The eighth sums up its heart as a discovery in two directions.
p120.s2.b7: The sixth and ninth directions shed light on the inner side of this life. The will of the finite creature and the will of the infinite Creator were to become as one in a single life, and while Michael would in fact live as an ordinary man, he would remain potentially a Creator Son. That is why, after his Adjuster came, he was to refrain from any superhuman will-to-power, and no superhuman repercussions were to attend his life apart from the will of the Father.
p120.s3.h: III. Further Counsel and Advice — What Not to Leave Behind
p120.s3.b0: The third section offers advice, worked out with Gabriel, on the lesser phases of Michael’s life. This counsel is a key that explains in advance why Jesus did some things and not others.

head: Area
Counsel
rows: Give attention to things practical and immediately helpful to your fellow men
Follow the accepted customs of home life in your day
Concentrate on spiritual regeneration and intellectual emancipation; avoid economic and political entanglement
Do not interfere with normal evolution, but leave an uplift of religious ethics
You may identify with existing movements, but avoid establishing an organized cult
Leave no writings behind, and let no images or likenesses be made of you
Honorable, but a bestowal Son leaves no human offspring
Left to the Adjuster’s leading, the spirit’s teaching, and the reason-judgment of the human mind

p120.s3.b3: The advice to leave no writings or images was given to prevent idolatry and crystallized religious systems. Immanuel also says that this life would not necessarily seem perfect to any one generation, yet would be supremely replete as judged on more perfected worlds. Having finished his charge, he took up the rule of Nebadon as acting sovereign and committed to Gabriel the safekeeping of the Son of Man about to be.
p120.s3.b4: The charge ends in blessing. Immanuel prays that the Father will guide and sustain Michael from the moment he surrenders consciousness, through his gradual recognition of his divine identity, until his ascension to the Father. When he had finished, Michael vanished in the presence of all.
p120.s4.b0: Those who had accused Michael of selfishly seeking rulership were left silenced before the self-forgetful service of the Son of Man, lived all the while in subjection to the Father’s will. The charge of rebellion was answered not by argument but by a life.

head: Misunderstanding
What the text says
rows: A dual-origin being, but not a double personality
He did not progressively become God
He became man at some moment

The human mind’s self-conscious realization of being God and man

p120.s4.b3: The author compares this mystery to the Trinity. Just as the Paradise Trinity of three beings is in reality one Deity, so God and man in Jesus were, and are, one. What grew in this relationship was not Jesus’ nature but the human mind’s awareness of it. Whoever reads the life of Jesus, then, is invited not to search for the moment divinity began, but to follow how one human being came to recognize who he was.
p120.s4.b5: To citizens of the local universe, the most intriguing miracle is the incarnation of a Paradise Son. Yet even in this extraordinary event, the Father chose the ordinary way, as he always does. As we read the life of Jesus, we are guided to see God first in natural, everyday life rather than in dazzling wonders.
p120.s5.b0: Paper 120 is a guide for reading the life of Jesus. Why he came as a baby, why he stayed clear of politics and economics, why he left neither writings nor images, why he chose weakness over power—all of this is already contained in this charge. And at the center of every choice stands unbroken communion with the Father.

p120.s5.b2: In the next paper, Paper 121, “The Times of Michael’s Bestowal,” a secondary midwayer once assigned to the Apostle Andrew portrays the political, social, and religious background of the first-century world that became the stage for this bestowal.
p121.lead: Roman roads, the Greek language, Jewish synagogues: the political, social, philosophic, and religious world into which Michael was born, and how the Gospels came to be written.

p121.foot.text: Narrated by a secondary midwayer once assigned to the Apostle Andrew

p121.s0.h: Introduction — The Story of Jesus, Told by Andrew’s Midwayer
p121.s0.b0: With Paper 121 the narrative of Jesus’ life begins in earnest. The narrator is a secondary midwayer once attached to the Apostle Andrew, working under the supervision of a commission of twelve members of the United Brotherhood of Urantia Midwayers. He is authorized to record the life of Jesus as it was observed by his order and as it was partly written down by Andrew himself.
p121.s0.b2: This brief opening shows that the counsel Immanuel gave in the previous paper—to leave behind no writings and no images—was in fact honored. The other apostles took a similar attitude, and so the writing of the Gospels was long delayed. Before the story of Jesus begins, the paper first unrolls a map of the world into which he was born.
p121.s1.h: I. The Occident of the First Century after Christ — The Most Favorable Time
p121.s1.b1: At the time of his birth Urantia was experiencing a revival of spiritual thinking and religious living unmatched in all its post-Adamic history. The narrator says that the world then offered the most favorable condition for a Creator Son’s bestowal that had ever existed before or has existed since. Western civilization was unified under three great influences, and one man, Paul, illustrates the whole combination well: a Hebrew of the Hebrews who proclaimed the gospel of a Jewish Messiah in the Greek tongue while himself a Roman citizen.

head: Influence
What it supplied
rows: Political and social systems, good roads, a unified empire, seas cleared of pirates
Language and culture—and philosophy to a certain extent
Rapidly spreading religious and moral teachings, with more than two hundred synagogue communities across the empire

p121.s1.b3: Yet beneath the internal peace and surface prosperity, most of the empire’s inhabitants lived in squalor and poverty. A small upper class was rich, and a happy, prosperous middle class had only just begun to appear. These were the real conditions of the people whom the gospel would seek out.
p121.s2.h: II. The Jewish People — Crossroads of Three Continents
p121.s2.b0: Palestine was the crossroads of three continents. The travel, trade, and armies of empires from Babylonia to Rome swept over this land in turn, and the caravan routes from the Orient passed through it to the seaports of the eastern Mediterranean.
p121.s2.b2: Under Roman suzerainty the Jews still enjoyed considerable self-government, and remembering the deliverance won by Judas Maccabee, they longed for a still greater deliverer, the Messiah. They took the good fortune of keeping their independence among stronger powers as proof that they were the “chosen people.” That sense of racial superiority made Roman rule all the harder to bear, and they refused to learn that their world mission was spiritual, not political.
p121.s2.b3: Herod the Idumean built temples for strange gods, but he also built the harbor of Caesarea, which helped make Palestine the crossroads of the civilized world. His son Antipas rebuilt many Galilean cities, including the trade center of Sepphoris. When Jesus was born, Galilee was more gentile than Jewish and did not enjoy the full favor of the religious leaders in Jerusalem.
p121.s3.h: III. Among the Gentiles — A Society of Five Strata
p121.s3.b0: First-century Mediterranean society consisted of five well-defined strata. Half the population of the Roman state were slaves, and the early Christian church was largely composed of the lower classes and these slaves.

head: Stratum
Description
rows: The privileged ruling groups, with money and official power
Merchant princes, bankers, and international traders
Few in number but influential, the moral backbone of the early church; many Pharisees belonged here
Proud of being free, yet competing with slave labor and held in low regard
Half the population; the more capable could earn their freedom and rise to higher rank

p121.s3.b2: Interestingly, people were generally content with their social rank and did not regard class distinctions as unjust. The narrator states plainly that Christianity was not a movement for correcting the economic lot of the depressed classes. The gospel turned first to the inner person, not to the structure of society.
p121.s4.h: IV. Gentile Philosophy — A Way for the Strong and the Wise
p121.s4.b0: Morally the gentiles were somewhat behind the Jews, but in the hearts of the nobler gentiles lay abundant soil of natural goodness and human affection in which the seed of the gospel could sprout. The gentile world was then dominated by four philosophies, all more or less derived from Platonism.

head: School
Teaching
Limits and contributions
rows: The pursuit of happiness; men can improve their earthly lot
A controlling Reason-Fate rules nature; virtue is its own reward
Rose to a sublime morality, but remained a philosophy and never became a religion
Simplicity, virtue, and fearless death—remnants of Machiventa Melchizedek’s teaching
Preached in fields and markets, preparing the common people for later missionaries
Knowledge is fallacious; certainty is impossible
Purely negative, it never spread widely

p121.s4.b3: The Stoics sought to attune their minds to the harmony of the Universal Mind, but they never pictured themselves as the children of a loving Father. Here lies the difference between philosophy and religion. Lofty principles can discipline a person, but they cannot open a relationship with the Father.
p121.s5.h: V. The Gentile Religions — The Mystery Cults and Beyond
p121.s5.b0: In earlier ages religion had been chiefly a tribal or national affair and did little to satisfy the personal longings of the average person. In Jesus’ day the West had pagan cults, emperor worship, astrology, and the mystery religions flooding in from the Levant. The mysteries were nonnational and fraternal, with elaborate initiation ceremonies, and they promised deliverance from evil and survival after death; they quickly won over the lower classes.
p121.s5.b1: The narrator reads the popularity of the mysteries as a real hunger for personal religion. They could not satisfy that longing, but they prepared the way for Jesus, who truly brought the bread of life. Paul adapted Jesus’ teachings to some extent to reach more people, yet even that compromise was superior to the best in the mysteries.

head: Compared
The mystery religions
Christianity as Paul preached it
rows: Moral redemption, ethical salvation, a new life and a new ideal
Deliverance from sin and a righteous character with survival qualities
The historic fact of the bestowal of Michael, a Son of God, upon mankind

p121.s5.b4: In the gentile world, moreover, morality was not necessarily tied to religion. The Jewish religion, the teachings of Jesus, and Paul’s Christianity were the first European religions to lay one hand on morals and the other on ethics, requiring believers to attend to both.
p121.s6.h: VI. The Hebrew Religion — Hellenized Judaism and Philo
p121.s6.b0: By the end of the first century before Christ, the religious thought of Jerusalem had been strongly shaped by Greek culture and philosophy. Three languages were in use in Palestine: Aramaic among the common people, Hebrew among priests and rabbis, and Greek among the educated. The Greek translation of the Hebrew scriptures marked the renaissance of Judaism, and it later became the decisive influence that turned Paul’s Christianity westward rather than eastward.
p121.s6.b1: Philo of Alexandria harmonized Greek philosophy and Hebrew theology into a fairly consistent system. The narrator counts him among the seven outstanding human teachers, with Sethard, Moses, Zoroaster, Lao-tse, Buddha, and Paul. Paul wisely removed many of Philo’s inconsistencies, but on the doctrine of the atonement he failed to keep pace with him: Philo taught deliverance from the doctrine of forgiveness only by the shedding of blood. The text adds that Paul’s theory of original sin and hereditary guilt was partly Mithraic in origin.
p121.s7.h: VII. Jews and Gentiles — The Fetters of Tradition
p121.s7.b0: The Jews had built a rigid wall of separation between themselves and the gentile world, and they indulged a self-righteousness founded on the letter of the law and the pride of descent. The Messiah they awaited was a deliverer who would arise out of their own national history. With such an outlook, it was very hard to receive Jesus’ teaching about the spiritual brotherhood of man.
p121.s7.b2: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and the Psalmist had spoken of a law written in the heart and a new spirit within, but a religion caught in traditionalistic inertia could not follow that path. So the motion of religious evolution passed westward to the European peoples, and Paul’s Christianity came to combine the philosophy of the Greeks, the law of the Romans, the morality of the Hebrews, and even the redemption doctrines of the mystery cults.
p121.s8.h: VIII. Previous Written Records — The Four Gospels and the Narrator’s Acknowledgment
p121.s8.b0: The narrator explains that, while drawing on Andrew’s lost record and on the help of many celestial beings, he has also aimed to make use of the four Gospels. He then describes in turn how each Gospel came to be written.

Completed near the end of A.D. 68, for the church at Rome

p121.s8.b2: Each of these writers gave an honest picture of Jesus as he saw, remembered, or had learned of him, colored by Paul’s theology. The narrator does not hide their imperfection, yet he recognizes their power.
p121.s8.b4: The acknowledgment at the end of the paper shows how to read all of Part IV. The narrator used human sources first wherever possible; only when they failed did he turn to the memories of the midwayers, and only when those failed did he resort to superplanetary sources. His memoranda gather the thought of more than two thousand human beings, because he believes that concepts born in human minds will prove more acceptable to other human minds.
p121.s9.b0: Paper 121 does not set the life of Jesus in a vacuum. He came into a world prepared with roads, a common language, and synagogues—a world whose philosophy was lofty but could not embrace the weak, and whose religions were many but could not feed the hunger of the individual. To that generation he gave his gospel of personal religion: sonship with God.
